text:
Two of Tampa Bay's four goals came on chances our numbers gave a 2% shot of going in. That is not a recipe anyone can repeat on purpose, but against a Chicago team that has forgotten how to win, it was plenty in a 4-1 Lightning win at Benchmark International Arena.

Victor Hedman started it on the power play at 4:12 of the first, with Anthony Cirelli and Brandon Hagel assisting. Ilya Mikheyev's snap shot at 18:22 was the first improbable one, a 2% look that beat Arvid Soderblom for a 2-0 lead. Ryan McDonagh's slap shot 2:38 into the third was the second. Mikheyev's tip-in at 5:08, a genuine 45% chance with Erik Cernak setting him up again, put the game away. Roman Kantserov tipped one in at 19:10 to spare Chicago the shutout.

Strip out the strange finishing and Tampa Bay was still the better team, just not by four goals' worth. Expected goals, the quality of each side's chances, ended 2.82 to 1.95 for the Lightning, and at even strength it was nearly level at 2.05 to 1.90. Replay every shot and Tampa wins 66% of the time. The real gap was in goal: Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26 and saved 0.95 goals more than expected, while Soderblom allowed 1.2 more than his 35 shots against deserved.

Cernak finished with two assists in 16:06, and Mikheyev, who reached the NHL undrafted after a 45-point KHL season with Avangard Omsk, had the kind of night that gets a forward a longer look. Nikita Kucherov had Tampa's best chance that didn't go in, a 25% look in the first.

For Chicago, it is five games without a win (0-4-1), and the second loss in two nights in Florida after Wednesday's game in Sunrise. The Blackhawks threw 31 hits to Tampa's 13 and won only 26 of 69 faceoffs. Hits are effort you can count; chances are what win games, and 1.95 expected goals was never going to test Vasilevskiy for long.
headline: Mikheyev scores twice as Chicago's slide reaches five
